title: Low-Power Inference Engine with Quantization-Aware Circuit Design
problem: Power consumption limits inference deployment on edge devices. Standard neural networks require high-precision arithmetic, increasing circuit power overhead and silicon area.
motivation: Edge devices require efficient neural network inference with minimal power overhead to enable practical on-device AI applications.
method: The paper co-designs quantization-aware training with circuit implementation to reduce arithmetic precision requirements. Quantized models use fewer bits for computation, enabling specialized low-power arithmetic units in the circuit. The inference engine implements ResNet-50 with optimized dataflow tailored to reduced-precision operations.
key_novelty: Co-design of quantization-aware training with specialized circuit arithmetic units to minimize power consumption in edge inference.
contributions: Quantization-aware training methodology for precision reduction
Specialized low-power arithmetic units exploiting reduced precision
15W power consumption achieved for ResNet-50 edge inference
Circuit-level optimization co-designed with quantized models
limitations: Scalability to larger models and comparison with other low-power inference systems not discussed.
primary_theme: Low-power inference through quantization-aware circuit co-design
